root_idea.summary: The root centers on keeping speech inward, concealed, or subdued: secret or suppressed utterance.
root_idea.development: From concealed or lowered speech, the lexical field extends to quietness and stillness, and in broader Classical Arabic to weakness, death, subdued natural phenomena, and several specialized uses.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form III perfect citation form.
Displayed under the normalized Form VI perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To speak or recite in a secret, low, or suppressed voice.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with speech or recitation when the utterance is deliberately subdued rather than openly voiced.

senses.definition: To speak secretly or quietly with one another; to confer in hushed tones.
senses.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or collective construction for people communicating among themselves in concealed or subdued speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a voice or speaker, to become still, silent, low, soft, or subdued; خَفْتٌ is speaking with a suppressed voice, including reciting indistinctly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to voices, speech, and recitation; a weak or dying speaker may be described as having ceased speaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become weak through vehement hunger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Specifically attested of weakness resulting from intense hunger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To die, especially to die suddenly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sudden-death usage is associated with the infinitive خُفَاتًا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become weak, abject, or abased.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A further Classical use of the verb, distinct from the sense of dying.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To silence or kill by a blow, such as a stroke of a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use reported of striking or smiting.
Specialized usage with camels as the subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to give birth on the day of the year in which she was impregnated, or about a year after covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized reproductive term applied to a she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feign or make a false show of weakness and stillness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or marked Classical use, separate from actual hushed conversation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low or depressed tract of ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a synonym of خَبْتٌ in one dictionary tradition.
Reported under differing vocalizations and in a variant dictionary account; the evidence contrasts this usage with the lowland meaning.
Attested as a specialized noun, reported from a tradition.
Used adjectivally or in an epithet expressing weakness and abasement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lean or emaciated woman, or one scarcely seen distinctly because of leanness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized epithet explicitly applied to a woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman regarded as goodly or beautiful, whose appearance attracts notice when she is alone but not when she is among other women.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An alternative specialized explanation of the same epithet, explicitly restricted to the described social comparison.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a cloud, lacking water and remaining in place, with at most faint or infrequent lightning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a cloud that does not travel like a water-bearing cloud.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of seed-produce, dying or dead, or stunted and not fully grown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The descriptions include produce that has not reached its full height; an alternative explanation describes it as fresh, juicy, soft, or tender.

cautions: The noun خَفْتٌ/خُفْتٌ has conflicting reported assignments: one account gives a low or depressed tract of ground, while another gives rue; both are retained as Classical alternatives.
The description of خَافِتٌ applied to seed-produce includes divergent reported interpretations, from dying or stunted produce to fresh, soft, or tender produce.
The specialized epithet خَفُوتٌ has competing Classical explanations concerning leanness versus beauty when a woman is viewed alone.
